newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: U.N. envoy hopes speed Timor talks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy hopes speed Timor talks.

text.p: The United Nations' special envoy for East Timor, Jamsheed Marker, said on Wednesday that he was hopeful of speeding talks between former colonial power Portugal and Jakarta on the troubled Indonesian-occupied territory.

Marker, making his first visit to Portugal since being appointed last month, said that he had come to hear the views of the Portuguese authorities on how to resolve the diplomatic dispute that threatens to cloud European and Asian relations.
"I continue to be optimistic...the negotiations are going to continue," he told reporters after meeting Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama.

A former Pakistani ambassador to the U.N., Marker was named as U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan's personal representative in a sign that the international organisation was stepping up the search for a solution to the problem of Timor.
Indonesia occupied the eastern part of the territory after the Portuguese withdrew in 1975 and annexed it one year later.
But its action was never recognised by the United Nations and Portugal has been pressing for the Timorese to be given the right to decide their political future.
Jakarta and Lisbon have had periodic meetings under the auspices of the U.N. but the talks have made little progress.

A session set for New York last December was cancelled to give Annan, a Ghanaian who only took over as secretary-general from Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali that month, more time to familiarise himself with the problem.
Marker, 74, was due to return to New York after his three-day stay. He goes to Jakarta at the end of the month for talks with Indonesian authorities.
